label: PF Backlog 499
title: Allocator defaults to the reachable local PF API authority + isolate the allocator store in tests
body:
Source: user request (2026-10-08) - "why did it get a block one / is the shared API not available?"

PROBLEM: the id allocator only uses the shared API authority when PF_API_URL is set; else it silently falls back
to LOCAL blocks (id-blocks.json). So the authority was never used even though a PF API was running - and two
worktrees each with their own id-blocks.json then collided. Also, tests that create items write into the REAL
config/id-blocks.json (it accumulated project::_test_* blocks) - test pollution + churn.

FIX:
- core/id_allocator._api_base(): default to the LOCAL PF API (http://$API_HOST:$API_PORT, default
  127.0.0.1:8000) when reachable (/health==200), short-TTL cached; explicit PF_API_URL always wins;
  PF_ID_ALLOC=off still disables. So the shared authority is used by default.
- test isolation: a conftest under test-framework/tests/pipeline sets id_allocator.OUT to a temp file so tests
  never touch the real store.
- reset config/id-blocks.json to empty blocks (drop the accumulated test-scope garbage).

Acceptance: with a local PF API up and PF_API_URL unset, add_epic reserves from the API; with the API down it
falls back to a local block; tests leave config/id-blocks.json byte-identical; no opencode/dashboard refs.

test:test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_id_allocator.py

brief.problem: the id allocator silently fell back to local blocks because PF_API_URL was unset, so the shared API authority was never used; and tests wrote into the real config/id-blocks.json
brief.what_adds: the allocator defaults to the reachable local PF API (health-checked, TTL-cached) so the shared authority is used by default; tests isolate the allocator store
brief.why: so concurrent sessions are coordinated by the shared authority instead of colliding, and the allocation store stays clean
brief.who_feels: sessions/agents that create backlog items; maintainers (clean store)

objective: the allocator uses the shared PF API authority when reachable and never pollutes the committed store from tests
acceptance_criteria: with a local PF API up and PF_API_URL unset, add_epic reserves from the API
with the API down, it falls back to a local block
explicit PF_API_URL wins; PF_ID_ALLOC_API=off disables the API path
in_scope: test isolation for the allocator store
out_of_scope: the worker claim path (it allocates nothing)
approach: PF_API_URL wins; else default to the local PF API when /health==200 (10s cache); PF_ID_ALLOC_API=off disables; tests set the allocator OUT to a temp file

existing_path: id_allocator._api_base returned empty unless PF_API_URL set
divergences: allocation now attempts the local authority by default

impact_review.recommendation: default to the reachable local API

risks: defaulting to a local API that is a different repo authority

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/artifact_store.py, core/asset_store.py, core/budget_allocator.py, core/forge_store.py

dashboard_impact.reason: allocator authority + test isolation; no dashboard surface
